hints: Notice the 50.0 cm distance from P to Q and that only the component of force perpendicular to bar PQ causes a moment about P.
For the 16.0 N force at $30^{\circ}$ to the bar, the perpendicular component is $16.0 \sin 30^{\circ}$, while the 5.0 N force is already marked perpendicular to the bar.

Check the rotational senses viewed from above: the perpendicular part of the 16.0 N force turns the bar one way about P and the 5.0 N force turns it the opposite way, so subtract their $F \times d$ moments.
walkthrough: Convert the length to metres: $d = 50.0 \text{ cm} = 0.500 \text{ m}$. Moment about P is $\text{force perpendicular to PQ} \times d$.
For the 5.0 N force, it is perpendicular to PQ, so $M_{5} = 5.0 \times 0.500 = 2.5 \text{ N m}$ in one rotational sense.
For the 16.0 N force, resolve perpendicular to PQ: $F_{\perp} = 16.0 \sin 30^{\circ} = 16.0 \times 0.5 = 8.0 \text{ N}$.
Its moment is $M_{16} = 8.0 \times 0.500 = 4.0 \text{ N m}$ in the opposite rotational sense to $M_{5}$.
Resultant moment magnitude is the difference: $M = 4.0 - 2.5 = 1.5 \text{ N m}$.
